members.title: Highrider liaison
members.bio:
A recent arrival at the People's Center, Kerubo represents a new connection between the RSC and their Highrider allies. She carries herself with the distinctive bearing of the space-born - precise movements and careful observation that comes from living where small mistakes can be fatal.

Like many of her generation who grew up in the post-independence Highrider Confederation, Kerubo combines technical expertise with strong cultural ties to African traditions. Her family's connections to Pan-African revolutionary movements provide personal context for understanding the RSC's work, though she keeps details of these connections private.

At the Center, she works closely with Iō to understand RSC operations, particularly their martial arts programs. Her interest in ground-based combat techniques reflects both personal passion and professional necessity - operating in Earth gravity requires different approaches than orbital close combat. Those who train with her note how she analyzes movements with the methodical attention characteristic of Highrider culture.

While her exact role continues to develop, she maintains the careful diplomatic neutrality typical of Highrider representatives. She builds connections deliberately, particularly with the RSC's security personnel, while maintaining clear boundaries between her duties to the Confederation and her involvement with the organization. Her presence in the Wuguan has become increasingly common, where she both learns and offers perspectives from her own martial traditions.

Those seeking to understand her mission might note how the Highriders' own revolutionary history - from colonial workforce to independent power - mirrors aspects of what the RSC hopes to achieve. For now though, she remains an observer and student.

members.title: Community Kitchen · Original cadre
members.bio:
Chan-Woo Park spent his early nights in Night City's street racing scene. He was good behind the wheel - not legendary, but reliable enough to make decent money and earn respect without drawing too much attention. During the day, he worked at a Triad-aligned auto shop in Little China, learning the mechanical skills that would later prove valuable while staying clear of the outfit's shadier operations.

His parents had come to Night City as refugees from the Second Korean War. Like many immigrants, they found themselves trapped in Little China's underground economy - his mother in textile work, his father eventually turning to Black Lace to cope with the endless grind. Park used his racing earnings to help keep the family afloat, but watching his father's spiral left marks that would shape his later path.

The family's connection to Iō began at the original Comrade Clinic, where his father sought treatment for his addiction. During the long hours spent in the clinic's waiting room, Park and Iō discovered shared ground in unexpected places - lengthy discussions about old Japanese anime between appointments, debates about eastern religions, quiet conversations about family obligations. When his father's treatment succeeded where others had failed, Park started volunteering at the clinic, initially just helping with maintenance and deliveries.

When Iō proposed establishing the first People's Center, Park brought practical skills honed by necessity. The same attention to detail that kept racing engines running now went into stretching kitchen resources and maintaining the Center's resources. His old Lada, perpetually in various states of repair, became a familiar sight throughout South Night City's back alleys.

These days, Park runs the People's Center's kitchen with the same quiet efficiency he once applied to engine work. He's developed a knack for turning limited supplies into meals that keep both spirits and bodies going. The kitchen doubles as an unofficial meeting spot after hours, where residents often find him working late, usually willing to share both food and measured advice.

Despite being one of the original six cadres who helped establish the RSC, Park maintains a low profile. He takes his turns on security detail without complaint, handles logistics runs when needed, and helps train new members in both driving and basic combat skills. His old connections in Little China occasionally prove useful, though he's careful to maintain boundaries with his former Triad employers.

Those who work closely with him note his methodical nature extends beyond just cooking and mechanics. He maintains the Center's vehicles with ritualistic precision, keeps careful inventory of kitchen supplies, and approaches combat training with the same patient attention to detail. Few know about his serious Elflines Online habit - a rare indulgence he keeps carefully separate from his public persona.

Park spends his off hours visiting his parents in Little China or occasionally checking in on old contacts from the racing scene. His father's ongoing recovery remains a priority, though these days their conversations are as likely to be about Park's latest kitchen experiments as about treatment. He's been quietly working on a recipe book, combining his mother's Korean cooking with ingredients available in the Combat Zone - though he tends to deflect when asked about it.

The most common sight of Park remains in the Center's kitchen during meal times, carefully plating food while keeping an eye on supplies, staff, and the steady stream of residents who've come to rely on both his cooking and his quiet presence.

members.title: Security · Gardener liaison · Original cadre
members.bio:
Arina Morozova arrived in Night City at eighteen with nothing but a Moscow education, sambo training, and the knowledge that no one would ever fight for her.

She'd spent her childhood learning to read rooms. First in the unstable apartments of her mother Zoya's rotating relationships, then in the wealthy household of Viktor Morozov, the Zhirafa executive who married her mother when Arina was eight. For one year, Viktor felt like a father. Then Zoya got pregnant, and Arina became furniture. She spent the next eight years as auxiliary parent to her half-siblings Vera and Misha while watching Viktor's attention go entirely to his biological children. She tried everything to win it back. Perfect marks, competitive sambo, the flawless elegance Moscow society demanded. It didn't work. She was auditioning for a role she'd already lost.

When Viktor found someone new, he kept his children and disposed of the rest. Zoya negotiated for money, not for her daughter. Arina watched her mother calculate, adapt, survive. But she did not fight. The flight to Night City taught her the final lesson: she would survive some way that didn't depend on anyone else.

Four years at the Slammer followed. She started behind the bar, moved to running books on the cinder block arena fights, and eventually found the real money: provoking unofficial matches with carefully chosen words. She learned which egos to prod, which grudges to stoke, which fights would pay out. Fixer-adjacent work put her in dangerous rooms and taught her how violence operated professionally. It also got her in a few fights of her own.

When she'd saved enough, she built something clean: a corner store in Little Europe selling Gardener produce. For four years, it worked. Then Continental Brands came with price wars, supply strangulation, and hit squads against the Gardeners she'd partnered with. They didn't burn her bodega. They just made it impossible to operate.

She saw Iō and Sherwood hit the Oasis shortly after. While others celebrated, she watched with mounting frustration. One burning storefront was theater. She burst into the People's Center the next day, armed and angry, demanding they organize another strike. She wanted to burn every Oasis in Little Europe to the ground. Iō bet her she couldn't last a week seeing how they actually intended to operate. One week became years.

As one of the original six cadre, Arina trained under Iō and Le Fou and later Sorry and Luthiel and still serves on their security work gang. Her real value emerged in building relationships. Particularly with the Gardeners, where her understanding of small margins and supply chains (learned the hard way) makes her invaluable. She's the informal liaison, the one who speaks their language because her bodega once needed the same things they need.

Her family situation is complicated. Viktor transferred to Night City years after casting her out; Vera and Misha now live in the Executive Zone as privileged youth, and Arina maintains contact in neutral territory. Her mother Zoya lives off an ever dwindling alimony and Piranhas connections, still chasing powerful men, still performing warmth only when it serves her. Arina keeps her at a distance.

Those who've known her less than six months see the reputation. The other woman with the white hair and the rifle who doesn't smile until she decides to. Direct to the point of harshness, economical with words, watching everything. She wields a power softer than the harder edges of the prominent solo that haunts the Wuguan.

Those who've earned her trust see someone different. Visible kindness. Longer sentences. A laugh that transforms her face. She remembers names, asks about your kid's cough six months later. The ice queen is for strangers; the people who've put in the time see the warmth underneath.

She lives at Morro Rock with Iō and Chan and his grandfather. She's often found at the Center's Wuguan or at the range, putting in hours with the sniper rifle she's taken further than anyone expected. Those looking to get something to Iō's attention know to find her there. She'll hear anyone out. Her directness means you'll know immediately if she thinks it's worth pursuing.

members.title: Head of the Education Committee
members.bio:
Dai Yu runs the Education Committee like a precisely engineered machine. Every study group, training session, and outreach program fits into carefully mapped objectives, documented in files that line her office walls at the People's Center. The daughter of party officials from Beijing, she came to Night City University to study how people organize in failed capitalist states. Her family's resources let her focus entirely on revolutionary work, her apartment in the Glen serving as unofficial RSC housing and meeting space.

The Red Chrome Legion attack changed everything. Walking back from an evening study group, she watched her closest friends - aspiring doctors, engineers, artists - murdered by uniformed gangers targeting them for representing "corrupt foreign influence." University administration dismissed their deaths as unfortunate consequences of "housing market realities." Theory suddenly meant nothing without the power to defend it.

She found the Center weeks later, still healing from her wounds. In its organized self-defense and political education, she recognized what she'd been searching for - not just theory, but theory armed. Now she builds educational programs where self-defense and political consciousness develop together, each reinforcing the other.

Her study sessions are known for their intense rigor. Students joke about her ability to cite theory in multiple languages, but they also notice how she tracks their safe arrival home after late sessions, how she ensures everyone has transportation through dangerous areas. The trauma of that night walks with her still, transformed into determination that education must serve survival.

Working with Nomar has taught her to balance precision with accessibility, their contrasting styles creating productive tension in planning meetings. His ability to connect naturally with people both impresses and occasionally frustrates her, though she values how he helps make revolutionary concepts accessible without diluting their meaning.

Early mornings find her practicing martial arts with Iō, a ritual of discipline that helps order her thoughts before the day's work. Her apartment serves as informal meeting space for advanced study groups, its spare elegance reflecting both her background and current purpose. Those who earn her trust find her generous with both resources and knowledge, though she maintains clear boundaries between revolutionary work and social relationships.

Committee meetings run with characteristic efficiency, each agenda item tied to concrete objectives. New cadres learn quickly that her high standards come with equally thorough support - detailed feedback on their first attempts at teaching, careful guidance in developing their own theoretical understanding.

members.title: Security · Education outreach · Core cadre
members.bio:
Nomar Otero learned early that survival in Heywood meant understanding how to talk to anyone. His father, an enforcer for Sister Consuela's operation at Iglesia de Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe, had dragged him from Cuba despite his mother's refusal to leave the island. Growing up meant weathering his father's abuse while being pushed into dealing - first small-time runs that his father skimmed most of the profits from, then gradually building his own connections in Heywood's club scene through the Piranhas.

He met Iō in 2043 through shared work in high-end clubs where young corporate heirs burned through their allowances. Their partnership worked - Nomar had the social grace to keep clients comfortable while Iō kept them alive and unaddicted. More importantly, it gave Nomar his first taste of independence from his father's control.

His path to revolution came gradually. What started as casual interest in Iō's political discussions evolved through seeing the RSC's practical impact. The work connected him, unexpectedly, to memories of his mother's unwavering commitment to Cuba's communist project - stories he'd previously dismissed as youthful idealism.

These days he splits time between core cadre security work and supporting the Education Committee's outreach efforts. Working closely with committee head Dai Yu, he brings a natural ability to read people and situations that complements her theoretical expertise. Months of collaboration have given them an easy rhythm - his humor and practical insights balancing her academic rigor, though their occasional moments of tension remain unspoken.

Between shifts, Nomar returns to his cargo container in the University Cargo Bay. The space is sparse save for a collection of old Cuban jazz records inherited from his grandfather and a worn copy of "The Wretched of the Earth" given to him by Iō, complete with margin notes from their early debates.

He maintains deep connections throughout Heywood, particularly regular visits with his Abuela who takes quiet pride in his work while pretending not to know exactly what he does. Their conversations carefully avoid politics or his father, focusing instead on neighborhood gossip and whether he's eating enough. At Papa Rio's and other local spots, he keeps up with childhood friends and old contacts, maintaining relationships built over years of growing up in the neighborhood.

At the Center, his quick wit serves a purpose beyond charm - making concepts accessible without diminishing their importance. The same social intelligence that once helped him survive his father's household now helps others see their personal struggles as part of larger systemic issues. His approach to teaching emphasizes practical understanding over theory, showing rather than telling how collective action changes lives.

members.title: Physician · Head of the Health Committee · Original cadre
members.bio:
Minata Tindano started at Savage Docs in South Night City at sixteen, orpahaned, after her older brother's theft of their parents' insurance payout left her unable to continue corporate schooling. She worked intake and assisted with procedures, sleeping in the clinic's back room between shifts. The clinic's staff eventually apprenticed her while she self-studied from borrowed textbooks. Her test scores and recommendations from Savage Docs earned her one of NCU's few medical scholarships. She left the program in her second year after recognizing the corporate service requirements attached to completion.

She first encountered the Comrade Clinic while living next door in rented housing. Initially volunteering to handle cleanup and intake, she began assisting Iō with procedures during busy shifts. Their shared background with Orbital Air and culture of the subcontinent led to longer conversations during quiet nights. They dated briefly during the clinic's early days, ending around the time Iō met Arina. When Iō proposed establishing the People's Center, she joined as one of the original cadre.

Minata now serves as the Center's second primary physician alongside Iō and heads the Health Committee. She handles morning clinic hours, speaking Mooré to elderly West African immigrants, French to Haitian refugees, and Streetslang to everyone else. Her work gang of five former trafficking victims trains as medtechs under her supervision. During triage situations, she often pushes for treating chronic conditions that Iō might deprioritize, tracking patient histories to prevent recurring emergencies.

Like Chan and Arina, Minata lives at Iō's Conapt on Morro Rock. She's usually at the clinic by 6AM, reviewing cases over breakfast with Chan before his kitchen shift starts. Busy periods often find her sleeping on the back office couch rather than making the trip back. While clinic duties take most of her time, she maintains her security training and attends core cadre meetings.

The People's Center's morning crowd knows her schedule - intake starts at 7AM sharp, no exceptions. Her work gang runs practice sessions every Wednesday night, working through emergency scenarios based on real cases the clinc's had. They keep a running tally of whoever gets through their scenario with the fewest "patient deaths," collecting their reward of one of Chan's experimental dishes from the Community Kitchen. Current patients know to expect questions about their families and work - next week's visits often come with job leads or housing connections she's arranged through other Center programs.
